programme: RFXAP driving the RFX/CIITA MHC-II transactivation module (HLA-DR/DP/DQ/DM/DO, CIITA) for antigen presentation, feeding a T-cell response that TOX marks as it shifts toward exhaustion/checkpoint status under chronic antigen exposure, with PKNOX1 (targets include IL10, CCL2, PTPN6, PF4) shaping the surrounding cytokine/myeloid microenvironment that determines whether that T-cell response is sustained or suppressed
role_in_a: In Colon_and_Rectal_Cancer, RFXAP-driven MHC class II machinery underlies CD4 T-cell infiltration (mutation in HLA class II-regulatory genes tracks with infiltration, PMID 25445815); that infiltration is checked by an immunosuppressive, macrophage-remodeled stroma (PMID 41274349) in which TOX-marked exhaustion and PKNOX1-linked cytokine signaling (PMID 40625743, PMID 36566600) operate.
role_in_b: In lower_grade_glioma_and_glioblastoma, the same TOX and PKNOX1 nodes are flagged in pan-cancer analyses as an immune-checkpoint marker and a prognostic immunological biomarker respectively (both from PMID 39152366 and PMID 40625743), consistent with glioma's well-characterized T-cell exhaustion and myeloid-dominated immunosuppressive microenvironment; no direct literature or Open Targets hit places RFXAP/MHC-II itself in glioma in this record.
shared_axis: Both tumor types can present antigen and provoke a T-cell response that becomes checkpoint-restrained (TOX) and is shaped by an immunosuppressive cytokine/myeloid milieu (PKNOX1-linked targets) regardless of tissue of origin, so an antigen-presentation-to-exhaustion axis recurring across CRC and glioma patient groups is biologically plausible as convergent tumor immunology rather than shared organ biology.
reasoning: The module is nameable and internally coherent, and TOX and PKNOX1 are each placed in both diseases by retrieved papers (mostly the same pan-cancer analyses), which is more than pure inference; but no paper in the record ties CRC and glioma together through this axis specifically, RFXAP itself (the module's structural anchor and its highest-support factor at 188/437) has zero glioma evidence, and the reader's overall note flags most of the supporting literature as thin or unjudgeable, so this falls short of an established or strongly evidenced connection.
support: PMID 25445815 - RFXAP-associated HLA class II regulatory gene mutations track with CD4 T-cell infiltration in colorectal cancer; PMID 41274349 - MARCO+ macrophages drive immunosuppressive remodeling in colorectal liver metastases, the stromal context TOX operates in; PMID 39152366 - TOX proposed as a pan-cancer immune checkpoint, including glioma, by pancancer analysis; PMID 40625743 - pan-cancer analysis identifies PKNOX1 as a prognostic and immunological biomarker spanning both colorectal cancer and glioma; PMID 36566600 - tumor-suppressor inactivation study supporting a colorectal role for the PKNOX1-adjacent pathway.
how_to_falsify: In matched CRC and LGG/GBM cohorts, stratify tumors by RFXAP/MHC-II target expression and TOX expression: if high-MHC-II/high-TOX tumors show no difference in cytotoxic T-cell activity, checkpoint-blockade responsiveness, or PKNOX1-linked cytokine output (IL10, CCL2) versus low-expressing tumors in both cancers, or if perturbing PKNOX1 fails to move myeloid infiltration and cytokine output in parallel CRC and glioma models, the shared-axis account is wrong.
caveats: 437 patient-group comparisons rest on only 2 independent cohort pairs, so within-cohort pseudo-replication likely inflates apparent recurrence. RFXAP's obligate complex partner RFX5 and the Treg master regulator FOXP3 were both removed as tissue-generic, so this account cannot invoke a full RFX5-RFXAP-RFXANK trimer or Treg-driven suppression — only the isolated RFXAP-MHC-II link survives. Nine of the twelve concordant factors (CDX4, UBTF, CEBPZ, JARID2, CRX, HINFP, HCFC1, MAZ, TFAP2C) sit outside this immune axis entirely — cell-cycle/ribosome-biogenesis factors or tissue-mismatched developmental regulators such as the photoreceptor factor CRX and intestinal CDX4 — and are not part of this story. Open Targets records no association at all for RFXAP, UBTF, CEBPZ, JARID2, HINFP, HCFC1, MAZ, TFAP2C, or CDX4 in glioma.
